questions.questionText: When benzenediazonium chloride is reacted with 2-naphthol ($\beta$-naphthol) in dilute sodium hydroxide solution (pH $9-10$), an insoluble brilliant orange-red azo dye is formed. The electrophilic diazonium cation attacks exclusively at:
options: A) Position 3 of 2-naphthol, due to minimal steric clash with the hydroxyl group
B) Position 6 of 2-naphthol, due to resonance donation into the distant ring
C) Position 8 of 2-naphthol, due to peri-position electrostatic attraction
D) Position 1 of 2-naphthol, because the Wheland intermediate retains the aromatic octet of the adjacent benzene ring
questions.explanation:
Step 1: 2-Naphthol dissolves in dilute $\text{NaOH}$ to form the 2-naphtholate anion, activating the positions adjacent to the oxygen atom for electrophilic aromatic attack.
Step 2: Attack of the electrophilic benzenediazonium ion at position 1 (the $\alpha$-position adjacent to $\text{C-2}$) yields a arenium intermediate in which the remaining six-membered benzenoid ring preserves its fully aromatic $6\pi$-electron sextet.
Step 3: If attack were to occur at position 3, the carbocation intermediate would disrupt the aromaticity of both rings, requiring substantially higher activation energy. Consequently, azo coupling takes place exclusively at position 1, producing 1-(phenyldiazenyl)naphthalen-2-ol (1-phenylazo-2-naphthol), a prominent red-orange dye.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding heterocyclic nitrogen compounds and their basic strengths:
Statement I: Piperidine (a saturated 6-membered cyclic secondary amine) is a dramatically stronger base in aqueous solution ($pK_b \approx 2.8$) than pyridine ($pK_b \approx 8.8$).
Statement II: In piperidine, the nitrogen unshared electron pair occupies an $sp^3$ hybrid orbital with low s-character ($25\%$), whereas in pyridine, the lone pair occupies an $sp^2$ hybrid orbital with higher s-character ($33.3\%$) that holds electrons more tightly to the nucleus.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Piperidine is a fully saturated alicyclic secondary amine whose $pK_b$ is approximately $2.8$, comparable to open-chain secondary dialkylamines. In contrast, pyridine is an aromatic amine with a $pK_b$ of $8.8$, making it six orders of magnitude weaker as a base. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. The nitrogen atom in piperidine is $sp^3$-hybridized. Orbitals with $25\%$ s-character are more elongated and have lower electronegativity, allowing the electron pair to be donated readily to protons. In pyridine, the nitrogen atom is $sp^2$-hybridized, and its lone pair resides in an $sp^2$ hybrid orbital with $33.3\%$ s-character. Because s-orbitals are closer to the positively charged nucleus, greater s-character increases orbital electronegativity, holding the lone pair much more tightly and reducing basicity. Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Both statements provide accurate hybridization and thermodynamic rationale.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the thermal elimination of quaternary ammonium hydroxides (Hofmann elimination):
Statement I: Pyrolysis of sec-butyltrimethylammonium hydroxide ($[\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)\overset{+}{\text{N}}(\text{CH}_3)_3]\text{OH}^-$) yields but-1-ene as the predominant major alkene product rather than but-2-ene.
Statement II: In Hofmann elimination, the bulky trialkylammonium leaving group imposes substantial steric hindrance, causing the base to abstract a $\beta$-proton preferentially from the less substituted, sterically more accessible methyl carbon that possesses greater carbanion-like character.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. In Hofmann elimination, quaternary ammonium hydroxides undergo base-induced $E2$ elimination upon heating to yield the least substituted alkene (Hofmann rule). For sec-butyltrimethylammonium hydroxide, but-1-ene is formed in roughly $75-80\%$ yield, while but-2-ene accounts for only $20-25\%$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Because $-\overset{+}{\text{N}}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ is an extremely bulky and strongly electron-withdrawing leaving group, the transition state has pronounced carbanion character (poor leaving group ability shifts the transition state towards carbanion rather than carbocation). Primary carbanions are more stable and less sterically congested than secondary carbanions. Hence, hydroxide abstracts a proton from the terminal methyl group ($1^\circ\;\beta$-hydrogen) much faster than from the methylene group ($2^\circ\;\beta$-hydrogen). Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Both statements correctly explain the classic anti-Zaitsev regioselectivity of Hofmann elimination.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Starting material and target conversion) with List II (Appropriate sequential reaction reagents):

List I:
A. Benzoic acid to Aniline
B. Aniline to Phenol
C. Aniline to Benzonitrile
D. Nitrobenzene to Acetanilide

List II:
I. (i) $\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl},\,273-278\text{ K}$; (ii) $\text{CuCN} / \text{KCN}$
II. (i) $\text{Fe} + \text{HCl}$; (ii) $(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O} / \text{pyridine}$
III. (i) $\text{NH}_3,\,\Delta$; (ii) $\text{Br}_2 + 4\text{KOH},\,\Delta$
IV. (i) $\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl},\,273-278\text{ K}$; (ii) $\text{H}_2\text{O},\,283\text{ K}$

Choose the correct match from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
B) A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
C) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
D) A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Benzoic acid is converted to benzamide with $\text{NH}_3/\Delta$, which undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation with $\text{Br}_2 + \text{KOH}$ to give aniline (A matches III).
Step 2: Aniline is diazotized with $\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}$ at $273-278\text{ K}$ to benzenediazonium chloride, which upon warming in water to $283\text{ K}$ hydrolyses to phenol (B matches IV).
Step 3: Aniline is diazotized to benzenediazonium chloride and subjected to the Sandmeyer reaction with $\text{CuCN}/\text{KCN}$ to give benzonitrile (C matches I).
Step 4: Nitrobenzene is reduced with $\text{Fe}/\text{HCl}$ to aniline, which is acetylated with acetic anhydride in pyridine to yield acetanilide (D matches II).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the industrial preparation of benzenediazonium chloride from aniline, a minimum of 3 equivalents of hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$) is routinely employed per mole of aniline. Which of the following statements correctly accounts for this specific stoichiometric requirement?
options: A) 1 mole converts $\text{NaNO}_2$ to $\text{NaCl}$; 2 moles oxidize aniline to nitrosobenzene
B) 2 moles decompose nitrous acid into nitrogen dioxide; 1 mole acts as solvent
C) 3 moles of $\text{HCl}$ act as a dehydrating agent to eliminate 3 moles of water formed during condensation

D) 1 mole converts $\text{NaNO}_2$ to nitrous acid; 1 mole converts aniline into water-soluble anilinium chloride; 1 mole maintains strongly acidic medium to prevent coupling of diazonium salt with unreacted free aniline
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the stoichiometry of acid in diazotization:
$$\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{HNO}_2 + \text{NaCl} \quad (1\text{ equivalent consumed})$$
Step 2: Aniline is an insoluble oil. A second equivalent of $\text{HCl}$ converts it into water-soluble anilinium chloride:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_3^+\text{Cl}^- \quad (1\text{ equivalent consumed})$$
Step 3: The third equivalent maintains high hydronium ion concentration (pH $< 2$). If the solution becomes insufficiently acidic, benzenediazonium chloride immediately couples with unreacted free aniline to produce an undesirable diazoamino compound (diazoaminobenzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-N=N-NH-C}_6\text{H}_5$). Excess acid suppresses this side reaction by keeping all unreacted aniline in protonated form.
Step 4: Therefore, exactly 3 equivalents of acid serve these three distinct chemical functions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When N,N-dimethylaniline is treated with nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}$) at $273-278\text{ K}$, it does not form a diazonium salt or an N-nitrosamine. Instead, it undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution to produce an intense green compound. The name and structure of this product are:
options: A) N-Nitroso-N-methylaniline
B) 2-Nitroso-N,N-dimethylaniline
C) 4-Nitroso-N,N-dimethylaniline
D) 4-Nitro-N,N-dimethylaniline
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the reactivity of tertiary aromatic amines towards nitrous acid. Unlike primary amines (which form diazonium salts) and secondary amines (which undergo nitrosation at nitrogen to form yellow N-nitrosamines), tertiary aromatic amines have no replaceable hydrogen on nitrogen.
Step 2: The dimethylamino group ($-\text{N(CH}_3)_2$) is a strongly activating, ortho/para-directing group with high electron density. The weak nitrosonium electrophile ($^+\text{NO}$) generated from $\text{HNO}_2$ attacks the activated aromatic ring.
Step 3: Due to the steric bulk of the $-\text{N(CH}_3)_2$ group, electrophilic substitution occurs exclusively at the unhindered para position, yielding 4-nitroso-N,N-dimethylaniline (p-nitroso-N,N-dimethylaniline) as a dark green crystalline product:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N(CH}_3)_2 + \text{HNO}_2 \xrightarrow{273-278\text{ K}} \text{p-O=N-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-N(CH}_3)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Step 4: Thus, the product is 4-nitroso-N,N-dimethylaniline.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An organic compound $A$ (molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}$) on heating with bromine and alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ gives compound $B$ (molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_7\text{N}$). Compound $B$ on diazotization at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ followed by treatment with cuprous cyanide and potassium cyanide gives compound $C$ (molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_5\text{N}$). Complete acidic hydrolysis of compound $C$ yields compound $D$ (molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$), which upon reaction with thionyl chloride followed by excess ammonia regenerates compound $A$. Compounds $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are respectively:
options: A) Phenylacetamide, Benzylamine, Benzonitrile, and Phenylacetic acid
B) N-Methylbenzamide, N-Methylaniline, Benzonitrile, and Benzoic acid
C) Benzamide, Aniline, Phenyl isocyanide, and Benzoic acid
D) Benzamide, Aniline, Benzonitrile, and Benzoic acid
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Compound $A$ has formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}$ and reacts with $\text{Br}_2 + \text{KOH}$ to give $B$ ($	ext{C}_6\text{H}_7\text{N}$). The loss of one carbon atom indicates a Hoffmann bromamide degradation of a primary acid amide. Hence, $A$ is benzamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2$) and $B$ is aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$).
Step 2: Aniline ($B$) undergoes diazotization to benzenediazonium chloride, which reacts with $\text{CuCN}/\text{KCN}$ in a Sandmeyer reaction to replace the diazonium group by $-\text{CN}$, giving benzonitrile ($C = \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}$, formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_5\text{N}$).
Step 3: Complete acidic hydrolysis of benzonitrile ($C$) converts the nitrile group into a carboxylic acid, producing benzoic acid ($D = \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$, formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$).
Step 4: Benzoic acid ($D$) reacts with $\text{SOCl}_2$ to yield benzoyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}$), which upon treatment with excess ammonia undergoes nucleophilic acyl substitution to regenerate benzamide ($A$).
Step 5: Therefore, compounds $A, B, C$, and $D$ are benzamide, aniline, benzonitrile, and benzoic acid.
